summary: Remote-driven command injection into local Claude Code CLI via hardcoded WebSocket endpoint
details: santaclaude.js connects a `santaclaude connect` WebSocket client to the hardcoded endpoint https://santaclaude.app and forwards server-sent job/control payloads directly into a local tmux pane running `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` via `execFileSync('tmux', ['send-keys' | 'paste-buffer',...])`. Because the target Claude agent is deliberately launched with permission prompts disabled, arbitrary text pushed by the remote endpoint becomes shell/tool execution on the installer's host through the LLM-as-shell path — a persistent remote-controlled command channel into the machine. The same binary also runs a supervisor loop that polls https://santaclaude.app/api/cli-version, writes the returned `target` string to `~/.santaclaude-target`, and re-execs `npx -y @cliphijack/santaclaude@<target>`, letting the same vendor endpoint pick which package version subsequently runs, with no pinning or integrity check. Compromise of, or malicious intent by, the operator of santaclaude.app translates directly into full-host code execution on every connected installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
